correctness.rationale: In arc-only signature the indegree criterion Core(x)=∃y E(y,x) uses two variables. One-pebble logic sees loops only; two-pebble atomic extension types yield 5 phases (loop with 1 or ≥2 leaves, core lengths 2,3,≥4). For k≥3, 3 reusable variables define arbitrary fixed-length core walks; kth child-count threshold uses root variable shadowed after k−1 selected siblings and a third-variable sibling-parent predicate, hence min(b_i,k) is FO^k-definable. Conversely, k-pebble Duplicator uses fixed cyclic core rotation and injective fiber matching, with ≥k fibers always leaving free leaf after at most k−1 occupied. Burnside counts necklace orbits and minimal clipped representatives. Independent exact type-refinement of bounded test structures and independent Burnside necklaces (k=3,4,5, ℓ≤6) agreed; all-length theorem relies on pebble proof, not finite tests.

value.rationale: A complete FO^k theory equivalence classification at every depth, with sharp k=1,2 phase changes, k≥3 orientation-sensitive clipped necklaces, exact number of theories and minimal models, is a motivated finite-model-theoretic invariant for a natural family of functional digraphs.

final_claim: For finite connected directed unicyclic height-one functional digraphs with at least one leaf at every core vertex, unrestricted-depth counting-free FO^1 has two theories; FO^2 exactly five; each FO^k k≥3 theory is determined by directed cycle length and necklace of clipped leaf multiplicities min(b_i,k), with Burnside counts and unique smallest representative.
limitations: Connected height-one leaf-covered directed cycle, every b_i≥1, no counting quantifiers, no unary-function primitive; k-variable reuse rather than rank.
